clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by sections 301 and 426 (c) of the 
Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amend­
ed, Executive Order No. 10266 of June 
30, 1951, Entitled “ Suspension of Cer­
tain Provisions of the Officer Personnel 
Act of 1947, as Amended, Which Relate 
to Officers of the Navy and Marine 
Corps,” is hereby revoked.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10563 (signed 1954-09-25 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-09-28, 2:14 p.m.; 19 FR 6297, Federal Register of September 30, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10563.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: one sentence, which under sections 301 and 426(c) of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947, as amended, revokes Executive Order 10266 of June 30, 1951 (suspension of certain provisions of that Act as they relate to officers of the Navy and Marine Corps). The order has no recital, effective-date wording, deadline or condition. First end: the revocation is a one-time act, so it was performed when the order took effect. With no effective-date wording the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1954-09-25; that reading is an inference from the signature block, and the filing date 1954-09-28 is the alternative. The consequence, that Executive Order 10266 no longer suspends the Act, is a completed result and not a command that continues. Later instruments: a scan of every held order text for the bare number 10563 found only the order's own copies, the next order printed in the same issue (EO 10564) and unrelated page numbers; none amends or revokes it. Held EO 10365 (signed 1952-06-24) states that it supersedes Executive Order No. 10266 of June 30, 1951, so far as that order relates to the suspension of certain provisions of the Officer Personnel Act of 1947; that supersession concerns the target of this order's revocation and not this order, so it is not an end of EO 10563 and is disclosed as an earlier event affecting what the revocation accomplished. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

Held EO 10365 (1952-06-24) superseded the target, EO 10266, in part before this order issued; it does not name EO 10563 and is not an end of it. Nothing held amends or revokes this order later.","independent_command_check":"The order has no command other than the revocation.","savings_check":"None stated; the revocation is a performed act with no continuing command.","scope_check":"One clause, the revocation sentence; no partial effect is held or found."}
